# Idempotent APIs and large-file submission

## Start with one representative question

[S02-Q018](#S02-Q018)

<p>How would you make an API operation idempotent when clients retry or repeatedly send the same logical request?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Preserve the intended import or API effect when the same logical operation is submitted or executed again.</p>

<ul>
<li>Define operation identity, repeated-submission responses and conflicting payload handling.</li>
<li>Separate job deduplication from duplicates within the input and stored records.</li>
<li>Choose atomic or partial-success import semantics and expose status and row errors.</li>
<li>Trace concurrent resubmission and crash/retry boundaries with a verification plan.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [HTTP contracts, validation and MVC state](aspnet-http-contracts.md)
- [Background processing across replicas](aspnet-background-jobs.md)

<p>The idempotent API question first asks what counts as the same operation and what repetition means. The source import scenario applies that boundary to a complete flow: submission, validation, writing and reporting. A job can be unique while its records still conflict, and a retry can cross a persistence boundary. Keep those separate so the import design can satisfy all ten source constraints without treating any named technology as the answer.</p>

### S02-Q018 · Failure cases

<p>How would you make an API operation idempotent when clients retry or repeatedly send the same logical request?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q018](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q018)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q018](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q018)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you make an API operation idempotent when clients can retry or spam the same request?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Idempotency concerns the effect of repeating a logical operation. Define sameness and caller-visible behavior, including simultaneous submissions rather than only sequential retries.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Protect an operation invariant across retries and concurrent submissions.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the business effect, identity scope, retention period and persistence boundary; deliberate request spam is included but rate limiting is a separate concern.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Define identity reuse with identical and conflicting payloads.</li>
<li>Trace concurrent calls and a failure after persistence, and specify a distinguishing test.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Using a process-local duplicate check as a guarantee across replicas or equating idempotency with abuse prevention.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What happens when one operation ID arrives with different data?</li>
<li>What response should a retry receive while the first attempt is still running?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-SC001 · Production decision

<p>Design a flow for importing a file containing tens of thousands of records, from submission to an observable final outcome.</p>

**Source:** [S02-SC001](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#large-file-processing-scenario)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-SC001](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#large-file-processing-scenario)**

Open the source link for the complete original constraints. The scenario remains one source unit; its original Markdown is also preserved in the shared inventory.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Keep file submission, job execution and record-level correctness distinct. Explain one coherent design that meets every source constraint and exposes its failure boundaries.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Integrate import correctness, asynchronous processing and recovery into one defensible design.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>All ten source constraints apply: do not hold HTTP open until processing finishes; stream/chunk where appropriate; validate format and business rules; choose all-or-nothing or partial success; perform efficient bulk writes; produce a validation/error report; prevent repeat-file duplicate jobs; prevent duplicate records within the file and against stored data; expose status; make retries safe. Queues, jobs, SqlBulkCopy, EF bulk operations, unique constraints and idempotency are options, not prescribed answers; specify versions/providers and verify any chosen guarantees.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Map every constraint to an owned state transition and explicit failure policy.</li>
<li>Trace concurrent resubmission, invalid rows and a crash near persistence; propose evidence for correctness and throughput.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Solving only upload latency while ignoring row duplicates, partial failure or retry behavior.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would the report identify rows already committed under partial success?</li>
<li>What happens if the same file arrives again while the first import is running?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Agent-added production exercise: two replicas receive the same import while its first attempt is running. Some rows duplicate one another and others conflict with existing data; a worker crashes near a committed write, and the caller retries after losing a response. Using the source scenario’s ten constraints, define operation and record identities, choose atomic or partial success, draw job/status/report transitions, and propose tests for conflicting payloads and recovery. Add throughput measurements as a plan, not an observed result.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Defines idempotency and distinguishes submitting a file from writing its records.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Protects stated business effects under concurrent and repeated execution; separates job and record correctness; explains transaction/reporting choices and checks all source constraints.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A unique operation ID alone does not establish a safe import. Need concurrency and crash traces, row-level outcome examples, and tests of the actual persistence boundaries.</p>
